hero.oneLiner: Lucknow-based IVD company that develops, manufactures and markets diagnostic reagents, kits and POC devices and manufactures/imports/distributes diagnostic instruments B2B to diagnostic labs, hospitals and medical colleges.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Lucknow-based IVD company that develops, manufactures and markets diagnostic reagents, kits and POC devices and manufactures/imports/distributes diagnostic instruments B2B to diagnostic labs, hospitals and medical colleges.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Q-Line develops, manufactures and markets a diverse range of reagents (kits and POC devices) and consumables, and manufactures/imports/distributes diagnostic equipment, supplying since 2013 - directly or via distributors - mainly to diagnostic service providers, hospitals and medical colleges. Core IVD segments are Clinical Chemistry, Haematology, Immunodiagnostics, Molecular Diagnostics and Others (POC devices and Rapids); FY25 standalone revenue of Rs 31,371 lakhs split Reagents 56.27%, Instruments 36.64%, Consumables/Spares 4.47%, Service 2.62%. It runs a B2B model across around 26 states/UTs with exports, manufacturing from owned Lucknow plants and leasehold Delhi (Bawana) units, and makes analysers in India under technical collaborations with international companies.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:
- Q-Line Iris Private Limited — Subsidiary (w.e.f. Dec 07, 2023): Radiology & imaging services; incorporated 2023 as growth strategy
- Q-Line Innovations Private Limited — Subsidiary (w.e.f. Mar 07, 2025)
- Q-Line Nutraceuticals Private Limited — Former subsidiary (ceased Mar 24, 2025): Common directorship remains
- POCT Science House Private Limited — Former associate (ceased Mar 20, 2025): Diagnostic labs; controlling stake sold in FY25 to focus on core business; Rs 1,060 lakhs corporate guarantee still outstanding on its behalf
- POCT Services (partnership firm) — Promoter partnership (Saurabh Garg, Amita Garg): Promoter litigation disclosed includes proceedings of this firm
- Q Line Healthcare Private Limited — Common directorship
- Heidelco Medicore Private Limited — Common directorship
- ASG Buildtech Private Limited — Common directorship
- POCT Quality & Skill Development Private Limited — Common directorship
- Mediquity Technologies Private Limited — Common directorship
- IQ Line Private Limited — Common directorship (Ayush Garg)

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Reagents:** Clinical chemistry reagents (64% of FY25 reagent sales), Haematology reagents (29%), Rapid/ELISA kits, HPLC reagents, Coagulation reagents, Molecular kits (RT-PCR, RNA extraction, VTM - COVID-era), POC strips, Microbiology reagents
- **Diagnostic Instruments:** Selectra Pro M medium-throughput fully automatic clinical chemistry analyser (manufactured under European collaboration), Clinical chemistry analysers, Haematology analysers, Traded analysers and POC devices
- **Make-in-India pipeline:** Selectra Pro XL high-throughput clinical chemistry analyser (prototype, with Elitech BV), Microlab 300 semi-automatic clinical chemistry analyser (prototype), Medonic M20 three-part haematology analyser (regulatory review), KC1 Delta coagulation analyser (with Stago, under review), InnoLyte electrolyte analyser (indigenous), Automated slide stainer (indigenous), Q-Count 5 five-part haematology analyser (under development)
- **Consumables/Spares:** Macro cuvettes with balls, Lab plastic plates, Laboratory plastic tip racks, Syringe pumps
- **Services:** Annual maintenance contracts on medical equipment sold

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Diagnostic service providers/labs (B2B)
- Hospitals
- Medical colleges
- Distributors - presence in ~26 states/UTs plus exports; Uttar Pradesh 72.25% of FY25 standalone sales, five focus states 87% of FY25 revenue

certifications.title: Certs (RHP)
certifications.body:
- ISO 13485:2016 (Lucknow plant, Khasra No. 3105, Amausi)
- cGMP implemented across all manufacturing facilities under a comprehensive QMS
- Periodic inspections/audits since 2021 by CDSCO, State Drug Authority, Intertek, URS Certification Limited and European regulatory agencies

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Backward-integrated into reagent manufacturing via in-house R&D (23 R&D personnel, 7.35% of permanent employees; R&D spend around 1% of revenue; reverse-engineering of components); instruments are both manufactured in India under royalty-bearing Technology Transfer Agreements with global/European diagnostic companies (Selectra Pro M with royalty payable; haematology reagents with royalty on RFID tags; Stago for the KC1 Delta) and traded/imported. Key raw materials (chemicals, cubitainers/caps and packaging; instrument components such as Power Supply PT535, data cable tree, panel PC, measuring unit, temperature control board; bulk reagent, antigen, antibody enzymes substrates) are sourced from domestic and overseas suppliers with no long-term supplier contracts (prices negotiated per purchase order); purchases FY25: domestic Rs 5,689.59 lakhs vs international Rs 8,680.93 lakhs (FY24: 3,941.83 vs 11,707.65; FY23: 2,553.02 vs 7,169.71), indicating import dependence for raw materials. Forward: B2B model selling mainly through distributors (over 397 in FY25) and directly to diagnostic service providers, hospitals and medical colleges, on a purchase-order basis, supported by 93 sales personnel and 37 service engineers/field managers; product delivery dependent on outsourced logistics partners. Also positioning as a full-service CMO/CDMO for IVD, having reduced costs and sourced EOL components for three clients.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Mix shift to instruments: instrument share of revenue rose from 21.4% (FY23) to 36.6% (FY25) as own-manufactured analyser sales scaled from Rs 611 lakhs (FY24) to Rs 5,987 lakhs (FY25) alongside traded units
- Reagents remain the recurring-revenue anchor (56.3% of FY25 revenue), led by clinical chemistry (64% of reagent sales) and haematology (29%)
- EBITDA margin expanded to 22.73% in FY25 (18.48% FY24) but PAT fell to Rs 2,813 lakhs from Rs 3,445 lakhs and PAT margin halved to 8.97% - finance-cost and below-EBITDA drag as leverage rose
- Balance-sheet-funded growth: total borrowings rose to Rs 16,495 lakhs (FY25) from Rs 7,365 lakhs (FY23), D/E 0.87 vs 0.58; IPO earmarks Rs 11,000 lakhs for working capital
- Post-COVID normalization: molecular reagent sales collapsed from Rs 678 lakhs (FY23) to Rs 19 lakhs (FY25) and POC from Rs 264 lakhs to Rs 9 lakhs
- Geographic concentration: Uttar Pradesh contributed 72.3% of FY25 standalone sales; five focus states 87% of revenue

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Scale Make-in-India instrument manufacturing: take Selectra Pro XL and Microlab 300 prototypes through validation and approval; obtain approvals for Medonic M20 (haematology) and KC1 Delta (coagulation); develop indigenous Q-Count 5
- Commercially launch indigenously developed InnoLyte electrolyte analyser and automated slide stainer in H2 FY 2025-26
- Commission a fourth, reagents-focused manufacturing facility in Lucknow in FY 2025-26 to support growth
- Deepen penetration in focus states (Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Kerala, Odisha) under the B2B distributor-led model
- Focus on core IVD business - divested controlling stake in associate POCT Science House (diagnostic labs) in FY25

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: A fourth manufacturing facility, focused on reagents, at Plot C-42, Industrial Area Amausi, Lucknow is slated to begin operations in FY 2025-26 to support the growth trajectory; a further land parcel at KH-864 Amausi is held for future use. Existing capacity (~1,200 analysers and 1.4 million reagent kits p.a. across two owned Lucknow plants and leasehold Bawana, Delhi units) has been built up with plant & machinery additions of Rs 147.18 lakhs (2023), Rs 1,020.64 lakhs (2024) and Rs 334.89 lakhs (2025). Product-side expansion is via the Make-in-India analyser pipeline - haematology (Medonic M20, Q-Count 5), coagulation (KC1 Delta) and higher-throughput clinical chemistry (Selectra Pro XL) - pending validation/regulatory approvals; IPO proceeds fund working capital and debt repayment rather than plant capex.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- In-house R&D and reverse-engineering: 23 scientists/engineers (7.35% of permanent staff) driving prototyping and validation; R&D spend ~1% of revenue
- Three operating manufacturing facilities (two owned Lucknow plants commissioned 2018/2023, one leasehold Delhi-Bawana unit) with combined capacity of ~1,200 analysers and ~1.4 million reagent kits p.a.; ISO 13485:2016 and cGMP/QMS discipline
- Diversified IVD portfolio - reagents, instruments, consumables and AMC services across clinical chemistry, haematology, coagulation, HPLC, rapid/ELISA and molecular - marketed in ~26 states/UTs
- Technical collaborations with international OEMs (Elitech BV, Stago, other European partners) enabling Make-in-India instrument manufacturing to international quality standards
- 12-year brand build with promoter-led management: CMD Saurabh Garg has 31 years in healthcare/diagnostics; WTD Ajay Kumar Mahanty 20 years across sales, manufacturing and R&D
- Reagents-led model (56% of FY25 revenue) gives recurring consumable demand from installed diagnostic base

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Geographic revenue concentration in Uttar Pradesh — UP alone was 72.25% of FY25 standalone sales (focus states 87%); regional disruption or procurement shifts hit revenue directly
- Working-capital intensity and rising leverage — Borrowings more than doubled to Rs 16,495 lakhs by FY25 (D/E 0.87 vs 0.58 FY23); Rs 11,000 lakhs of the issue is for working capital and Rs 9,000 lakhs for debt repayment - growth is balance-sheet funded
- Dependence on international technical collaborations (Elitech BV, Stago, other European partners) — Key instruments are manufactured to partners' specifications; loss or adverse change in tie-ups would stall the instrument segment and the Make-in-India pipeline
- Large traded (non-manufactured) instrument component — Rs 5,507 lakhs of FY25 instrument revenue was traded goods, exposing margins and availability to third-party/import supply
- Regulatory approval and compliance risk — Medonic M20 and KC1 Delta launches depend on pending approvals; facilities face periodic CDSCO/State Drug Authority/ISO audits - delays or adverse findings defer sales
- Extensive promoter-linked entity web and legacy guarantees — Numerous group companies with common directorships; Rs 1,060 lakhs corporate guarantee outstanding for divested associate POCT Science House; promoter-level litigation exists
- PAT decline despite revenue and EBITDA growth — FY25 PAT fell to Rs 2,813 lakhs (margin 8.97% vs 16.92% FY24) even as revenue grew 54%, signalling finance-cost drag on earnings quality
- COVID-era product demand normalization — Molecular/POC revenue built during the pandemic has largely evaporated, showing demand for some lines is not durable

commitments.title: Promises (RHP)
commitments.body:
- **Commission a fourth, reagents-focused manufacturing facility at Plot C-42, Industrial Area Amausi, Lucknow, slated to begin operations in FY 2025-26.**
- **Introduce the indigenously developed InnoLyte electrolyte analyser and automated slide stainer into commercial sale in the second half of FY 2025-26.**
- **Obtain regulatory clearance for the Medonic M20 three-part haematology analyser (developed with a European partner) and expand the Make-in-India portfolio into haematology testing.**
- **Bring the Stago-partnered KC1 Delta coagulation analyser to market upon receipt of the requisite regulatory approvals.**
- **Advance the Make-in-India analyser pipeline: complete validation and formal approval of Selectra Pro XL and Microlab 300 prototypes (with Elitech BV) and develop the indigenous Q-Count 5 five-part haematology analyser.**
- **Repay certain borrowings, in part or full, using Rs 9,000 lakhs of issue proceeds.**
- **Deploy Rs 11,000 lakhs of issue proceeds to meet working capital requirements.**
